title: Proof of Structure of the defining boundary
html:
Proof. Proof of Structure of the defining boundary

(1). The descent map \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} is a surjective *-homomorphism of fibre algebras (descent). Its kernel is zero generically because the ascent \ell_n embeds A as a direct summand of J^1(A), with r_n acting as the left-inverse. The kernel is non-trivial only where this splitting degenerates—a closed algebraic condition on the Frobenius pairing \varepsilon \circ m. Since A is a Frobenius--Hopf object in a rigid monoidal category, standard vector-bundle degeneracy bounds give this locus a real codimension of at least 2.

(2). At a blow-up centre p \in \partial \mathcal{S}_n, \ker(r_n|_p) is the fibre of \Omega^1(A) over p modulo the image of \eta\colon \mathbf{1} \to A. Because \Omega^1(A) \hookrightarrow A \otimes A and A has fibre \mathrm{SU}(2), this quotient is isomorphic to the projectivisation of the 2-dimensional representation: \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \cong S^2. This yields the exceptional divisor resolving the singularity at p.

(3). The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} (descent involution) on J^1 \mathcal{S}_{n+1} restricts to the boundary locus \partial \mathcal{S}_n. Because \partial \mathcal{S}_n is defined by \ker(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}|_p) \neq 0 and \hat{\tau}_n projects onto the image of \ell_n, the restriction \hat{\tau}_n|_{\partial \mathcal{S}_n} acts as an involution. Its fixed points are the sections entirely within the descended subalgebra—matching the monodromy fixed-point condition of the quantum characteristic classes.

(4). At n = 1, the base is M and \mathcal{S}_1 fibres over M with fibre \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1) \cong S^2. The boundary \partial \mathcal{S}_1 marks the locus where jet restriction degenerates. By (2), each fibre of \partial \mathcal{S}_1 is \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}), separating base (spacetime) and fibre (chiral) coordinates. The Reeb vector field \xi is vertical, so the reversal \xi \mapsto -\xi exchanges the two sides of \partial \mathcal{S}_1. The positive Reeb eigenspace carries left-handed fermions, and the negative carries right-handed, realizing Descartes chirality.
